inputs.modified_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law after the American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with sincerely held beliefs. This looks like a coordinated reframing: turn abortion access into a religious-rights shield so legal limits can be portrayed as attacks on faith. LifeNews.com’s title—“This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right”—makes clear how sharply the ruling is being presented, but the larger move is to make a contested policy harder to challenge by wrapping it in religious freedom.
